intro: Chapter 5 of 1 Nephi turns from the sons' perilous errand back to the family waiting in the wilderness. Lehi's wife **Sariah** has complained bitterly against him — she feared her sons had perished on the road to Jerusalem and called him a *visionary man* — but when Nephi and his brothers return safely with the brass plates, both parents rejoice and offer sacrifice to the God of Israel. Lehi then searches the plates and finds on them the five books of Moses, a record of the Jews down to the reign of Zedekiah, the prophecies of the holy prophets including Jeremiah, and his own **genealogy** — which reveals that he is a descendant of **Joseph** who was sold into Egypt. Filled with the Spirit, Lehi prophesies that these plates will go forth to all nations and never perish or grow dim with time.

entries.title: Grammar: Compound verbs with کردن and شدن
entries.body: Persian builds most of its "verbs" by pairing a noun or adjective with a light verb — usually `کردن` _kardan_ "to do/make" (active) or `شدن` _šodan_ "to become" (inchoative/passive). The noun carries the meaning; the light verb carries person, tense, and mood. The chapter summary alone strings together five of them.
entries.closing: The imperfective `می-` here attaches to the light verb, not the noun. With `شدن` the same frame turns passive: `راهنمایی شدند` _rāhnamāyī šodand_ "they were led" ([verse 15](#verse-15)).

entries.title: Grammar: The object marker را
entries.body: The particle `را` _rā_ marks a **definite direct object**. It comes after the entire object noun phrase — including any ezafe chain, plural, or possessive — not after the bare noun. Persian word order is verb-final, so `را` is the reader's signal that the preceding phrase is the thing acted upon.

entries.title: Grammar: چنین گذشت — "and it came to pass"
entries.body: The Book of Mormon's signature narrative formula _and it came to pass_ is rendered `و چنین گذشت که` _o čonīn gozašt ke_ — literally "and thus it passed that." `گذشت` is the 3sg past of `گذشتن` "to pass," and `چنین` "thus" fills the English dummy _it_. The whole phrase simply advances the narrative to the next event; `که` "that" introduces the clause of what happened.

examples.en: And it came to pass that …
And it had come to pass that …
And it came to pass that …

entries.title: Grammar: Possessive and pronominal suffixes
entries.body: Persian attaches possession directly to the noun as an enclitic, with no separate word for "my/your/his." The set is `-am` (my), `-at` (your sg.), `-aš` (his/her), `-emān`/`-mān` (our), `-etān`/`-tān` (your pl.), `-ešān`/`-šān` (their). After a plural in `-ān` the linking vowel drops, giving `پسران‌م`, `پدران‌ش`, etc. The same clitics attached to a verb or preposition serve as object/oblique pronouns.

entries.title: Grammar: Ezafe chains
entries.body: The **ezafe** is an unstressed `-e` (or `-ye` after a vowel) that links a noun to a following possessor or modifier: `کتابِ من` "the book **of** me" = "my book." The Persian Book of Mormon usually does not write it, so this guide restores it as a small superscript kasra ( ِ ). Ezafe can chain indefinitely down a noun phrase, each link binding the next word.
entries.closing: When the head word already ends in `ۀ` (e.g. `نوادۀ`, `همۀ`) or in a long vowel spelled with `ی` (`سوی`, `خدای`), the ezafe is already written and this guide leaves it unmarked.

entries.title: Grammar: The past perfect (pluperfect)
entries.body: The pluperfect — English "had done" — is a **past participle** (`کرده`, `شده`, `دیده`) followed by the simple past of `بودن`: `بود`, `بودند`, `بودم` … It sets one past event before another, and it dominates this chapter, since Nephi narrates what Sariah _had_ said and feared before the sons returned.

entries.title: Grammar: Archaic narrative گفتا
entries.body: In the elevated biblical register, `گفتا` _goftā_ replaces plain `گفت` _goft_ "(he) said." The `-ا` is an old narrative/emphatic suffix once attached to third-person past verbs in classical poetry and story-telling; it lends the speech of Lehi and Sariah an archaic, scriptural dignity. Modern prose would simply write `گفت`. The suffix carries no extra meaning — subject and tense are unchanged.
entries.closing: Compare the same speaker's plain `سخن گفت` _soxan goft_ "spoke" ([verse 4](#verse-4)); the `-ا` form is reserved for introducing the quoted words.

entries.title: Grammar: The indefinite marker ـی
entries.body: An unstressed `-ī` suffixed to a noun marks it as **indefinite** — "a(n), a certain." It is the counterpart of English "a/an" and often pairs with a preceding `یک` "one": `یک مرد` … `مردی` both mean "a man." On a word ending in a vowel it appears as a separate `ای` (`نگاشته ای` "a record"). Do not confuse it with the possessive `-ī` "your" or the abstract-noun `-ī`.
entries.closing: When such an indefinite noun is followed by a `که` clause, the `-ī` becomes **restrictive** ("the … that"): `اندازه ای که` "such a degree that" ([verse 21](#verse-21)).

entries.title: Grammar: The future tense (خواهد + short infinitive)
entries.body: Formal Persian marks the definite future with the auxiliary `خواستن` "to want" — conjugated for person (`خواهم`, `خواهی`, `خواهد`, `خواهیم`, `خواهید`, `خواهند`) — followed by the **short infinitive** (the bare past stem: `داد`, `آورد`, `رفت`). Unlike every other compound tense the auxiliary comes **first**, and it takes no `می-`. Negation prefixes the auxiliary: `نخواهد`.
entries.closing: In everyday speech Persian usually drops this and lets the simple present carry future meaning; the `خواهد` future belongs to formal, scriptural, and written registers — exactly this chapter's prophetic tone.

entries.title: Grammar: The subjunctive after تا
entries.body: `تا` "so that, in order to" introduces a clause of **purpose**, whose verb must stand in the **subjunctive**. The subjunctive normally takes the prefix `بـ-` (`بگریزد`, `بروم`), but a compound verb usually drops it and leaves the bare present stem (`بدست آوریم`, not *`بدست بیاوریم`). It never takes `می-`.

entries.closing: The same subjunctive appears after other triggers of unrealized action — `که` "that" after verbs of wishing/commanding (`که او بتواند` "that he might", [verse 14](#verse-14)).

entries.title: Grammar: The passive voice with شدن
entries.body: Persian has no inflected passive. Instead it uses the **past participle** of the main verb plus a conjugated form of `شدن` "to become": `کشته شد` "was killed" (lit. "became killed"). Tense and person live on `شدن`; the participle is invariable. The agent, if named, is introduced by `به دست` or `بدست` "by the hand of."
entries.closing: The same participle-plus-`شدن` frame drives the passive of compound verbs: `راهنمایی شدند` "they were led" ([verse 15](#verse-15)).

etym.prose: from Hebrew _Ṣiḏqiyyāhū_ "Yah is my righteousness," via Arabic.
`پاد` pād "guardian, master" (Old Iranian _pati-_) + `شاه` šāh "king" → "protecting king."

entries.meaning: Judah (the southern Israelite kingdom; the patriarch)

etym.prose: from Hebrew _Yəhūḏāh_ "praised," via Arabic `یهودا`.

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 13 (`سیزده` — a single word, not "ten-three")

etym.prose: from Arabic, root q-d-s "to be holy, pure."
Middle Persian _dahān_; `از دهانِ …` "from the mouth of …" = spoken by.
from Hebrew _Yirməyāhū_ "Yah will exalt," via Arabic `إرميا`.

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 14 (`چهارده` — a single word, not "ten-four")

etym.prose: `خاندان` xāndān "family, dynasty, house" + `نامه` nāme "letter, document, record" → "record of the house."

entries.family: خاندان _xāndān_ family, lineage; نامه _nāme_ letter, document

entries.meaning: face, side; (in `از این رو`) for this reason, wherefore

etym.prose: variant of `روی` "face"; the idiom `از این رو` = "from this side" → "therefore, wherefore."
from Arabic `یعنی` "it means" (3sg of ʿ-n-y "to mean"), frozen as a connector.

entries.meaning: that same, the very, the selfsame

etym.prose: `هم` ham "same" + `آن` ān "that."
from Hebrew _Yaʿăqōḇ_ "he grasps the heel; supplanter," via Arabic `یعقوب`.
from Arabic/Hebrew `مصر` _Miṣr_, the Semitic name for Egypt.

forms.desc: past participle `فروخته` _forūxte_, in the passive `فروخته شد` "was sold" ([verse 14](#verse-14))

etym.prose: `خانه` xāne "house" + `وار` -vār "pertaining to" → "those of the house."
`قحط` qaḥṭ "drought, famine" (Arabic, root q-ḥ-ṭ) + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i).

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 15 (`پانزده` — a single word, not "ten-five")

etym.prose: from Arabic, root ʾ-s-r "to bind, capture"; an `اسیر` asīr is a captive.

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 16 (`شانزده` — a single word, not "ten-six")
in this, to this, by this (in `بدین گونه` "thus")

etym.prose: `به` be + `این` īn → "to/in this"; `بدین گونه` = "in this manner, thus."
Middle Persian _gōnag_ "color, kind"; `بدین گونه` / `این گونه` = "in this way."
`نگه` negah (variant of `نگاه` negāh "watch, guard") + `داشتن` dāštan "to hold" → "to hold in keeping."

forms.desc: past participle `نگه داشته` _negah dāšte_, in the pluperfect `نگه داشته بودند` "they had kept" ([verse 16](#verse-16)), `نگه داشته بودیم` "we had kept" ([verse 20](#verse-20))

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 17 (`هفده` — a single word, not "ten-seven")

etym.prose: from Arabic, root r-w-ḥ "breath, spirit"; `روحِ مقدّس` = "the Holy Spirit."

entries.meaning: to become; to turn, wander, roam

etym.prose: Middle Persian _wardīdan_/_gaštan_ "to turn"; as a copula it is a literary synonym of `شدن`.
from Arabic, root š-r-ʿ "to begin, set out"; `شروع به …` "to begin to …"

entries.meaning: to do, make; to show, display, appear

etym.prose: Middle Persian _nimūdan_ "to show"; a literary/formal synonym of `کردن` as a light verb.

forms.desc: 3sg past `نمود` _namūd_ "did, made," here light verb of `شروع` and `نبوّت` ([verse 17](#verse-17), [verse 19](#verse-19))

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 18 (`هجده` — a single word, not "ten-eight")

etym.prose: from Arabic, root m-l-l "religious community, nation."
from Arabic, root q-w-m "to stand; a people who stand together."
Middle Persian _mardōm_ "mankind" (← `مرد` mard "man"); grammatically singular but plural in sense.

forms.desc: 3sg past `رفت` _raft_ "went," also the short infinitive after the future: `خواهند رفت` "will go," `نخواهند رفت` "will not go/perish" ([verse 18](#verse-18))

forms.note: Suppletive present stem `رو` _rav-_ (e.g. `می‌رود` _mī-ravad_ "goes"). `از میان رفتن` = "to vanish, perish" ([verse 19](#verse-19)).

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 19 (`نوزده` — a single word, not "ten-nine")

etym.prose: Middle Persian _mayān_ "middle"; `از میان رفتن` = "to pass away, be lost."
← `گذشتن` gozaštan "to pass" (pres. `گذر` gozar-); `گذرِ زمان` = "the passage of time."
from Arabic `زمان` "time," root z-m-n.

entries.warning: Homograph: `تار` also means "thread, string; the _tār_ lute." Here it is the adjective "dim"; `تار شدن` = "to grow dim."

entries.meaning: Persian numeral 20 (`بیست` — a single word; multiples of ten are not composites)
here, this place; (in `تا اینجا`) thus far

etym.prose: `این` īn "this" + `جا` jā "place."
`بیست` bīst "20" + `و` o "and" + `یک` yek "1."

entries.meaning: to perceive, understand, realize; to receive

etym.prose: `در` dar "in" + `یافتن` yāftan "to find" → "to find out, grasp."

forms.desc: past participle `دریافته` _daryāfte_, in the pluperfect `دریافته بودیم` "we had perceived" ([verse 21](#verse-21))

etym.prose: ← `ارزیدن` arzīdan "to be worth" + the process-noun suffix `-eš`; `با ارزش` = "valuable."

entries.family: ارزیدن _arzīdan_ to be worth; ارزشمند _arzešmand_ valuable

etym.prose: Middle Persian _frazand_ "child, offspring."
← `خواستن` _xāstan_ "to want" + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-adjectival-suffix-i) → "worth wanting."
`بیست` bīst "20" + `و` o "and" + `دو` do "2."
`خرد` xerad "reason, wisdom" + [`-مند`](../word_formation.html#the-suffix-mand) "possessing" + [`-ی`](../word_formation.html#the-abstract-noun-suffix-i) → "the quality of the wise."

entries.meaning: likewise, still, as before; (in `همچنان که`) just as

etym.prose: `هم` ham "same" + `چنان` čonān "so, thus" → "in the same way."

entries.meaning: must, ought, to be necessary (impersonal modal)

forms.desc: `می بایستی` _mī-bāyestī_ "should, had to, ought to" — a past/modal form ([verse 22](#verse-22))

etym.prose: Old Iranian reflexive; `با خود` = "with oneself, along."

forms.desc: 1pl past `بردیم` _bordīm_, here `می بردیم` "we should carry" (past habitual/modal) ([verse 22](#verse-22))
